title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
gist: Toyota is reviving Scion as 'Scion by Toyota' and bringing the KEI-01 Kei truck to the US after Trump urged DoT to legalize Japan's Kei cars, but the KEI-01 is a 25 mph low-speed vehicle, right-hand drive only, and initially fleet-only, assembled from kits in Indiana. Ars frames US SUV dominance as a product of CAFE policy.

insights.claim: President Trump said last year he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan's Kei cars legal in the US, though DoT has given Ars little detail on any rule change.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Policy support for small imports is rhetorical so far; watch for DoT rulemaking.
insights.locator: The idea that Americans should be offered

insights.claim: The prevalence of huge SUVs in the US is largely a consequence of corporate average fuel economy standards that made smaller efficient cars less profitable, while Japan's Kei rules restrict size, engine capacity, and power.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Vehicle mix follows regulation; regulatory changes could reopen a US small-car segment.

insights.claim: Kei cars must be at most 3.4 m long, 1.5 m wide, 2 m tall, with engine displacement of 0.66 L or less and output of 63 hp or less, and Japan bought almost 1.7 million of them out of 4.6 million total vehicle sales last year.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Kei is ~37% of the Japanese market, a large proven segment.
insights.locator: A Kei car must fit within

insights.claim: Toyota is reviving its Scion sub-brand as 'Scion by Toyota' to experiment with less traditional ideas, showing KEI-01, SxS, and BKE concepts.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Toyota is creating a sandbox brand for niche mobility bets.

insights.claim: Toyota's KEI-01 will be classified as a US low-speed vehicle capped at 25 mph, offered only in right-hand drive with all-wheel drive and a 600 lb bed, and initially sold only to fleet buyers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Market is commercial/campus fleets, not mainstream consumers.

insights.claim: Toyota will assemble KEI-01 trucks at its Indiana plant from knock-down kits, adding 50 jobs in mid-2027.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Kit assembly gives a modest US manufacturing footprint, relevant to tariff/policy optics.
insights.locator: Oh, and it’s only available as right-hand drive

insights.claim: Toyota targets the KEI-01 at urban small businesses, farmers and ranchers, campus facility fleets, delivery drivers, and outdoor enthusiasts; pricing is unannounced, with speculation from $10,000 to $28,000.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Price point will decide whether it competes with golf carts/LSVs or utility vehicles.
insights.locator: Toyota says the KEI-01 is suited

insights.claim: The KEI-01 is not the consumer Kei car many US enthusiasts wanted, such as a boxy EV like the Honda N-One or Nissan Sakura.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Limited consumer impact from the 'Kei legalization' narrative for now.
insights.quote: You probably wanted a kei car like the Honda N-One. But that’s not what we’re getting.
